title: legal redlines scratchpad - enterprise inference contracts
content:
Quick scratchpad for redlines on enterprise inference deals (notes to self).

Context: negotiating reserved/dedicated + private deployment agreements with mid-market/enterprise customers. Focus on inference-specific risks (data, model outputs, uptime, audit access).

Clauses to watch / negotiate aggressively:
- Data use & retention: prohibit training on customer data. If customer data used for improvements, need explicit opt-in + anonymization + write-up of use cases. Add maximum retention window and purpose limitation.
- IP / outputs ownership: customer expects outputs belong to customer. Push for clear language: customer owns outputs and any derivative content they provide; provider retains model weights/underlying improvements.
- Security & access: require SOC2 Type II, yearly pen test results, and scope of access for support engineers. Add MFA requirement for any privileged access.
- Breach notification: 72 hours SLA for notification + remediation plan and cooperation obligations. Who pays for customer-facing notifications? try to limit to actual costs unless regulatory fines.
- PII / regulated data: disallow certain regulated categories (PHI, highly regulated financial data) in hosted API unless advanced controls. For Private/VPC, specify customer responsibilities and certification obligations.
- Subprocessors / third parties: need list + right to object; 30 days notice for material changes. Ensure flow-down obligations for security and breach notification.
- Indemnity: carve out for model outputs (we should avoid broad IP indemnities for model hallucinations). Counter proposal: indemnity limited to provider negligence and breach of confidentiality/security. Cap on liability equal to 12 months of fees (try for 6-12 months); carve out for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
- Warranty: limited warranty of service availability and compliance with specs. No warranty on accuracy of model outputs.
- SLA & credits: define measurable metrics (p95 latency, availability % for inference endpoints). Credits formula should be proportional and capped. Add right to terminate for repeated SLA misses after cure period.
- Termination & transition assistance: require 90 days transition assistance for enterprise + data export format and fees (reasonable). Provide option for short extension if export issues.
- Audit rights: scoped, quarterly or on reasonable notice; prefer remote audits and limit to security/compliance scope. Avoid unlimited on-site audits.
- Export controls & sanctions: include vendor right to suspend service for compliance with applicable laws; provide customer notice where possible.
- Source code escrow / escrow triggers: ask customer if they want escrow for Private on-prem deployments; set narrow triggers (bankruptcy, persistent failure to support).
- Pricing & usage overages: clear definition of token/embedding units, overage rates, burst vs reserved capacity. Add measurement and dispute window (30 days).

Negotiation talking points (short):
- We provide model runtime and infrastructure; we cannot guarantee factual accuracy of model outputs. Focus SLA on availability/latency rather than correctness.
- Data protections: we will not use customer data to train models without explicit consent. If customer wants continual improvements, offer paid opt-in program with strict controls.
- Liability: limit to fees paid; carve outs for gross negligence. Indemnity narrow to IP infringement from our software (not model outputs).
- Security: highlight SOC2 + pen test cadence and offer optional higher-security package for private deployments (HSM/KMS, dedicated encryption keys).

Open questions / action items:
- Check with infra (Jordan) whether we can commit to 99.95% for dedicated pools or if 99.9% is more realistic.
- Ask product (Maya) for exact definitions of token/embedding measurement method for billing disputes.
- Run indemnity language by outside counsel re: model-output carveouts.

References / quick links: Confluence checklist + standard contract template in repo. Keep this doc as live scratchpad during negotiation.

Notes to self: keep language simple for customer readability but include detailed defs in schedule. Save previous negotiated language snippets in repo for reuse.

End of scratchpad.
